content: H5N8 is a specific subtype of the Influenza A virus, which is often referred to as the bird flu virus. A highly pathogenic strain of this virus, identified as A/turkey/Ireland/1378/83, was responsible for a minor influenza outbreak in 1983 among turkeys in Ireland. The World Health Organization (WHO) has documented the need for a long-term response to avian influenza outbreaks, comparing the H5N8 outbreak to previous occurrences. This information was published in their Epidemic and Pandemic Alert and Response update on March 2, 2004. The European Commission's Scientific Committee on Animal Health and Animal Welfare released a report on June 27, 2006, discussing the definition of avian influenza and the role of vaccination in controlling the disease. This report was made available through the Health & Consumer Protection Directorate-General and retrieved on November 4, 2007. Further research on the virulence of avian influenza viruses has highlighted the importance of conserved amino acids at the cleavage site of the haemagglutinin protein. This was detailed in a study by Walker JA and Kawaoka Y, published in the Journal of General Virology in 1993 (Volume 74, Part 2, pages 311–314, PMID 8429306).
